records.detail: A collector reference site that catalogues notes printed in France says Djibouti's central bank is not part of the French banking system apart from the Banque de France printing its notes, and marks the printer field 'BdF' on the Djibouti entries it lists, running from the 500 and 1,000 franc notes of about 1979 through the 2,000 franc note of about 1999 and the 1,000 franc note of about 2005 to the 10,000 franc note of about 2009.
records.source_title: French Banknotes - French prints, Djibouti (Banque Nationale de Djibouti / Banque Centrale de Djibouti)
records.quote: other than Banque de France printing their banknotes

records.detail: A trade-press report on the launch of Madagascar's new ariary series on 17 July 2017 says the 20,000 ariary note, then worth about 6.80 US dollars, is printed on the Louisenthal hybrid substrate made by the German firm Giesecke and Devrient's paper mill. The report says the series uses several different substrates, and it does not say which company printed the notes.
records.source_title: Madagascar launches high-denomination banknote (Central Banking, 17 July 2017)
records.quote: is being printed on Giesecke and Devrient's (G&D) Louisenthal hybrid

records.detail: An encyclopaedia entry says this printing and refining company is wholly owned by the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, that its printing plant in the Msasa industrial area of Harare prints banknotes and other high-security government documents, and that it printed the 100 trillion Zimbabwe dollar note in 2008 during the hyperinflation years. The printer is reported here rather than confirmed by the central bank, and a separate press report of 6 December 2013 has the company's legal counsel saying it had not been instructed to resume printing the Zimbabwe dollar, so read this as the bank's own works rather than a current contract for the ZiG notes.
records.quote: The Highest note ever printed in the world was the Z$100 Trillion note Printed by Fidelity Printers and Refinery in 2008

confirmed_blank.note: Zambia stays a SUBSTRATE record and not a printer record; the lead is spent. The Heritage Series was issued by the Bank of Zambia on 31 March 2025 under section 17(1) of the Bank of Zambia Act 2022, and BanknoteNews records the printer as unknown for every denomination. The two 2012 rebasing reports show the bank had only INVITED tenders in February 2012, with bids due 23-28 March, and name no firm. The Currency News launch piece of 2 May 2025 is PAYWALLED and remains unread: round 66's agent reached it through a staging-host mirror of that publication, which is circumventing the paywall, so that reading has been discarded and the URL removed. DO NOT USE STAGING OR PREVIEW MIRRORS TO READ PAYWALLED PUBLICATIONS. If a paywalled piece is the only route to a fact, the fact stays unrecorded and is noted as paywalled. The IACA member page for the Bank of Zambia carries mandate and contact details and names no firm.

The one remaining monitorul.fisc.md lead was opened: https://monitorul.fisc.md/en/editorial/la-multi-bani.html names no printer, only the former governors Leonid Talmaci and Dorin Draguteanu whose signatures appear on the notes. A Romanian-language press search for the bank's banknote printing contracts returned only bnm.md node pages and opaque storage.mtender.gov.md download UUIDs, the routes already closed in earlier rounds.

Third refusal. The centralbanking.com lead was opened: 'Innovative print techniques are key for new Georgian banknotes', 2 February 2016, https://www.centralbanking.com/central-banking/news/2444659/innovative-print-techniques-are-key-for-new-georgian-banknotes names no firm, only 'a range of new security features, made possible by a variety of printing techniques'.

needs_a_hand_check.note: A possible De La Rue signal that a person should judge, not a source that states anything. The Banque Centrale de la Republique de Guinee hosts its own 10,000-franc recognition poster under the filename 41608-DLR-10000-Guinee-A2-Poster-V2.pdf at https://www.bcrg-guinee.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/41608-DLR-10000-Guinee-A2-Poster-V2.pdf , where 'DLR' with a five-digit job number is how De La Rue names artwork files, and the bank's other note artwork follows the same supplier-style naming (GIN_1000_Leaflet_V2_site.pdf, GIN_10000_Poster_A2_250506_WEB.pdf, poster_guinea_2024_07_sans-QR.pdf). The poster text itself credits only the issuing bank, so nothing in it states who prints the notes. Not filed: a filename is not a printing statement.

searched_no_result.note: Two French-language press and tender searches ('Banque Centrale de Djibouti billets impression marche imprimeur franc djiboutien' and 'La Nation Djibouti banque centrale nouveaux billets appel d'offres impression billets de banque') returned only the bank's financial statements and annual reports plus dealer catalogue pages, no tender or printing contract. The blog post on the 2017 40-franc commemorative note, https://commemorativenotes.blogspot.com/2018/02/djibouti-40-francs-2017-40th-year-of.html , only speculates that a different printer may have made it. The record filed above comes from the frenchbanknotes.com catalogue instead.

A Malagasy and French-language search for the 2017 ariary series printing contract returned no tender report. https://mriguide.com/large-new-madagascar-notes-to-be-issued-17-july names only the issuing bank, Banky Foiben'i Madagasikara, and its source, Midi Madagasikara. The printer of the ariary notes is still unknown; only the substrate for the 20,000 ariary note is on record.

Two further searches, one for the Heritage Series printer and one for a parliamentary or press account of who was awarded the printing, surfaced only launch coverage from Zambian outlets and the 2012 pre-tender reports listed under confirmed_blank. No Zambian source names the printer.

Vein 4 produced nothing this round. A site search for per-note 'Product Owner' profiles covering Djibouti, Guinea, Moldova, Madagascar or Zambia returned no such profile for any of them; the only currencyaffairs.org page for the five is the Bank of Zambia member page, which carries the bank's mandate and contact details and names no firm. The Wikipedia-derived 'List of banknote printers' mirror at https://cavac.at/cavacopedia/List%20of%20banknote%20printers was also read and mentions none of the five countries.

leads_not_opened.note: https://www.zimbabwenow.co.zw mirrors and mriguide.com pages on the ZiG notes were not opened; the current ZiG printer is still unrecorded.

https://platform.keesingtechnologies.com/zambias-new-family-of-banknotes-to-launch-on-march-31st/ and https://chalochatu.org/The_Kwacha_Heritage_Series were left unopened as late-round launch summaries unlikely to name a printer where the bank and Currency News do not.

The PDF file metadata of the BCRG's 10,000-franc poster was not inspected; even a De La Rue producer string would be an artefact of the file rather than a statement that the firm prints the notes, so it would still need a human decision.
